title: Jupiter Life Line Hospitals Ltd - 543980 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue INR456.5 crore, EBITDA INR106.9 crore, PAT INR56.4 crore; Dombivli EBITDA impact improved to INR0.2 crore from INR9.5 crore loss in Q1.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 income of INR456.5 crore, EBITDA of INR106.9 crore and PAT of INR56.4 crore, with H1 income INR867.5 crore, EBITDA INR186.2 crore and PAT INR93.9 crore. The board approved purchase of the Pune South leased land (11,452 sq m) for INR150 crore, with INR50 crore deposit adjusted, so incremental cash outflow is INR100 crore. Dombivli ramp-up improved sharply, helped by seasonally higher medical admissions in Q2, though management did not split out the seasonal effect. Indore EBITDA was flat despite about 18% top-line growth as medical teams are built ahead of the next bed addition.

financial_highlights.value: INR0.2 crore loss in Q2 vs INR9.5 crore in Q1
financial_highlights.change: improved by about INR9.3 crore QoQ

financial_highlights.value: INR600 crore (net debt about INR170-odd crore)

segments.name: Thane
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 75% (management also cited 70% earlier in the call), steady for the last couple of years as capacity nears saturation. Possible bed addition is subject to regulatory clearance, not yet received.

segments.name: Pune (existing)
segments.commentary: Occupancy close to 70%, leaving some headroom; management said no further bed expansion scope. Pune South greenfield project on schedule.

segments.name: Indore
segments.commentary: In growth phase with revenue up about 18% but EBITDA flat; medical hiring ongoing for the next several quarters. Next bed addition not expected for a couple of quarters, as occupancy is in mid-to-high 50s versus a mid-60s trigger.

segments.name: Dombivli
segments.commentary: Ramp-up continuing; occupancy about mid-30s currently. Not all specialties live: transplants to start in the next couple of quarters, radiation oncology under commissioning. No cashless empanelment yet; NABH application filed, insurance empanelment expected to take about a year.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give financial guidance; said new hospitals take about 2 years to reach EBITDA break-even, and Dombivli guidance will be revisited after 1-2 more quarters.
Q3 occupancy typically lower than Q2 in all units, so some moderation in Dombivli expected.
Maintenance capex about INR10-20 crore per unit per year as an average over 4-5 years.
EBITDA-to-operating-cash conversion averaged about 70%, may temper to 60-something if net debt rises.
Self-imposed debt ceiling of 3x EBITDA; company currently within it.
Over the next 2-3 years, ARPOB in new hospitals expected to rise faster than inflation as case mix matures; Thane ARPOB to grow only with inflation.
Mira Road to start next phase of construction before end of this financial year; BKC moving to regulatory clearance.
capex_capacity: Pune South: about INR220 crore spent so far, plus INR100 crore incremental for land; project on schedule.
Mira Road: land bought, about INR75-80 crore spent; in regulatory stage, capex to ramp once construction starts.
BKC: in planning stage, to enter regulatory clearance soon.
Indore: next bed addition not expected for a couple of quarters; occupancy must reach mid-60s first.
Secured INR500 crore term loan; INR100 crore earmarked for Pune South land, balance to fund the three live projects (Pune South, Mira Road, BKC).
demand_pricing: Q2 seasonally higher infectious disease admissions lifted Dombivli volumes; medical case mix dilutes ARPOB in Q2, as in prior years.
Dombivli occupancy about mid-30s currently; excluding Dombivli, H1 occupancy 64.8% (denominator based on about 144 census beds, not 200 total beds).
Insurance mix about 55% for the group; Dombivli lower because it lacks cashless empanelment, skewed to self-pay.
Fixed cost base at Dombivli about INR6-8 crore per quarter, may rise as beds and doctors are added.
Management did not provide ARPOB ex-Dombivli; only blended figures shared.
Oncology margin cap (30%) effective 1 November; management has not modelled the impact and may quantify by quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: Dombivli revenue and exit occupancy in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit-wise revenue not disclosed; occupancy currently around mid-30s percent.

qa_highlights.question: What would Dombivli losses be excluding seasonal benefit, and what Q3 loss to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot segregate the seasonal effect; Q3 occupancy typically lower than Q2 so some moderation expected, trajectory described as positive.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Supreme Court concerns on medicine markups and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Declined to comment on matters under deliberation; will abide by law of the land and has nothing new beyond prior statements on its community positioning.

qa_highlights.question: Indore EBITDA flat despite 18% revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth-phase investment in medical teams; expect fluctuations in top line, EBITDA and occupancy for several quarters; medical hiring ongoing for 2-3 quarters or more.

qa_highlights.question: Dombivli break-even timing and whether guidance will be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Typical budget model is 2 years of drag; too early to revise, will review after 1-2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Debt capacity for doubling beds?
qa_highlights.answer: Board has a self-imposed ceiling of 3x EBITDA on debt; currently within it.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion capex, maintenance capex, and balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: No new projects announced; maintenance capex INR10-20 crore per unit average over 4-5 years; end-H1 cash INR400-plus crore, gross debt INR600 crore, net debt about INR170 crore consolidated. No formal financial guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Dombivli specialties and ARPOB uplift from transplants and oncology?
qa_highlights.answer: Most specialties live; transplants in next couple of quarters, radiation oncology commissioning next quarter. ARPOB uplift not modelled; case mix expected to mature over 2-3 years.

risks_watch: Regulatory: oncology drug margin cap of 30% effective 1 November; EBITDA impact to be disclosed by quarter end; broader Supreme Court scrutiny of hospital pricing unresolved.
Dombivli: Q3 seasonal moderation in occupancy; insurance empanelment (NABH then insurers) typically about a year; fixed cost could rise with hiring.
Thane bed addition contingent on regulatory clearance not yet received.
Leverage rising with three live projects; net debt may increase, cash conversion could fall from about 70% to 60s.
Indore EBITDA volatility until medical teams mature and next bed phase fills.
Mira Road and BKC timelines subject to regulatory approvals.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating trajectory and balance sheet, but guarded and often non-committal on Dombivli timing, insurance empanelment, regulatory outcomes and quantified forward numbers; repeatedly declined to model seasonal effects or guide financially.
key_quotes: The overall ramp-up trajectory of Dombivli, however, remains intact.
We have always said that we prefer to own the land on which our hospitals are built as it gives us control, certainty, and better long-term financial value.
So, the board has currently mandated a self-imposed ceiling of 3x of EBITDA. We will not increase debt above that.
So, we have never given financial guidance, so I'll continue to refrain on that.
